Subject: Pre-close slotting: prioritization ask for Acme Analytics (ACME-314)

Team —

Quick heads-up ahead of ACME’s expected PO next week. They’ve signaled they’ll commit to a Dedicated pool to support their Q3 pilot + production ramp. High-level ask below; see attached spreadsheet (acme_capacity_request.xlsx) for the draft allocation and token forecasts.

What I need this week:
- Infra: confirm whether we can guarantee 48 vGPU-equivalent slots for their initial committed tranche (target start 2029-05-01). If not, provide a fallback (burst credits + expected latency impact).
- Finance: confirm billing cadence options (monthly vs quarterly) and whether we can accept the PO timing they suggested (PO expected by 2029-04-10).
- Sales: we need to lock on the reserve vs. on-demand mix to finalize pricing in SOW.

Summary numbers (from pipeline and ACME commercial team):
- Target committed GPUs (equiv): 48 initial, 120 within 6 months if pilot converts
- Expected average seq length: 1024 tokens; burst windows at EOD training workloads
- Revenue profile: $420k ARR in year 1 if full conversion

Links: HubSpot deal (ACME-314) attached; spreadsheet has week-by-week slot ask.

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 1 Apr 2029 13:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pre-close slotting: prioritization ask for Acme Analytics (ACME-314)

Thanks Jordan — tagging in infra and finance asks below. Quick notes from ops standpoint after a skim of the spreadsheet:

- 48 vGPU-equivalent steady-state is feasible in Q2 only if we hold the following safety buffer: 15% (to handle burst overshoot and model variation). With that buffer, we need to reserve 56 slots or provide guaranteed burst capacity of ~20% with pre-warm.
- If we commit to 56 slots reserved and their conversion to 120 in six months is realistic, we’ll need a tranche plan: 56 (May) -> 88 (July) -> 120 (Oct). Each step needs ~2 weeks ops lead time for provisioning + validation.
- Fallback strategy: maintain a cross-region fallback to EU for 24% of peak requests (if latency trade-offs are acceptable to ACME).

Can finance confirm whether we can tier billing (reserve base + burst overage) and whether a PO with a monthly cadence creates any provisioning timing issues?

Attaching quick ops notes to the spreadsheet and a short runbook stub I’ll use for handoff.

—Olga
Olga Petrov
Head of Capacity Planning, Redwood Inference
Attachment: acme_capacity_request.xlsx (see tab "ops_notes")
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 2 Apr 2029 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pre-close slotting: prioritization ask for Acme Analytics (ACME-314)

Quick finance readout —

We can support a tiered billing model: base reserved monthly charge + per-GPU-hour overage billed monthly. Two constraints:
1) For enterprise reserved pools we need at least a 3-month minimum commitment to cover fixed infra amortization unless sales agrees to a one-time uptake credit.
2) PO timing: our standard acceptance window to start provisioning is 10 business days after PO receipt + billing account validation, unless the deal team secures an expedited provisioning approval from the CFO.

Practical recommendation:
- Ask ACME to sign the SOW with a 3-month minimum for the initial tranche (56 slots). We can include an auto-escalation clause to increase to 88/120 based on pre-defined usage triggers (we can draft).
- If ACME insists on monthly-only terms without minimum, finance will require a 15% platform-initiation charge applied to the first invoice.

I’ve uploaded a redline of the SOW (named acme_sow_rev2.pdf) to the deal folder and added two billing cadence variants. Jordan — if you prefer, I can prepare a DocuSign-ready SOW with the tier we choose.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Director, Revenue Operations
Attachment: acme_sow_rev2.pdf
Related link: https://app.docusign.com/prepare/abc123 (draft)
From: Emily Park <emily.park@acme-analytics.com>

Date: Wed, 3 Apr 2029 17:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pre-close slotting: prioritization ask for Acme Analytics (ACME-314)

Thanks Jordan/Olga/Laura — appreciate the fast turnaround. A few points from procurement and product:

- Procurement timeline: PO ready by 2029-04-10 pending final SOW. We prefer monthly billing cadence but can accept a 3-month minimum if that meets Redwood’s provisioning requirements.
- Product note: we absolutely need the 56-slot minimum starting 2029-05-01 for our pilot KPI window. Latency to EU fallback is acceptable for non-interactive batch workloads but not for inference traffic during business hours.
- Can you confirm SLA impact if 20% of our requests are burst-routed to an alternate pool? We need expected p50/p95 latency deltas documented.

If you can send a DocuSign SOW with the 3-month minimum + auto-escalation triggers, we’ll push PO approval on our side. Attaching our internal procurement timeline (referenced in body).

Regards,
Emily Park
Head of Platform, Acme Analytics
Attachment: ACME_procurement_timeline.pdf (referenced)
